subject: Career
title: The Follow-Up: Where Relationships Begin
description: Learn The Follow-Up: Where Relationships Begin in one minute.

hook.text: You had a great conversation at a conference. You didn't follow up. Three months later, they've forgotten you.

buildup.text: The relationship doesn't start when you meet. It starts when you follow up.

discovery.text: The 48-hour rule: follow up within two days while memory is fresh. Reference something specific you discussed.

twist.text: Most people don't follow up. The ones who do stand out — not because they're better, but because they bothered.

climax.text: A simple message: 'Great meeting you. I loved your point about X. Let's stay in touch.' — done.

punchline.text: The meeting opens the door. The follow-up walks through it.

quiz.question: Why is the 48-hour follow-up rule important?
options: Memory is fresh and it shows you're serious about the connection

details.summary: The initial meeting is just the starting point; relationships are built in the follow-up. A thoughtful follow-up within forty-eight hours converts a momentary interaction into the foundation of a lasting professional connection.
details.whyItMatters: Most people fail to follow up after networking events, which means the small effort of doing so puts you in a distinct minority that stands out in the recipient's memory.
takeaways: Follow up within forty-eight hours while mutual memory is fresh
Reference a specific detail from your conversation for personalization
Offer something of value rather than immediately asking for a favor

faq.question: What is the best medium for following up after meeting someone at an event?
faq.answer: Email or LinkedIn message are both appropriate. Choose the medium where you have their contact information. LinkedIn is convenient because it reinforces the visual connection. Email allows for slightly more detailed follow-up.

faq.question: What should a networking follow-up message include?
faq.answer: A brief reminder of where you met, a reference to something specific you discussed, an offer of value like a relevant article or introduction, and a suggestion for staying in touch. Keep it under one hundred fifty words.
